case_title: State of Punjab v. Jagga Singh etc.
accused_occupation: Driver (accused Charanjit Singh, as described in the prosecution case noted by the Court)
accused_victim_relationship: Acquaintance (defence version, not decided by the Court): accused Charanjit Singh was known to the victim's mother and had worked under the victim's partnership
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302; IPC s.120-B; Arms Act s.25
weapon: Two country-made .303 pistols with live cartridges (firearms)
evidence_type: Eyewitness; fingerprint (latent prints on glass tumblers); medical (autopsy); recovery of pistols, cartridges, scooter and footwear; identification by witnesses
confession: Alleged extra-judicial confession by accused Ranjit Singh to PW9; not relied on because it was uncorroborated and PW9 had no authority to receive it
trial_court_outcome: All seven convicted. Two: IPC s.302 (life imprisonment and Rs.2000 fine each) and Arms Act s.25 (two years RI and Rs.1000 fine each). Five: IPC s.302 r/w s.120-B (life imprisonment and Rs.2000 fine each).
high_court_outcome: Allowed appeals of five accused and acquitted them; dismissed appeals of two accused and confirmed their conviction and sentence
offence_finally_established: Murder (IPC s.302) and Arms Act s.25 for the two accused; the five acquittals on s.302 r/w s.120-B were upheld
neutral_facts: On the early morning of the occurrence, two visitors who had arranged by telephone the previous evening to be taken to a plot for earthwork came to the victim's house. They were let in, and tea was prepared for them at the victim's direction. The visitors asked the victim to accompany them on his scooter. As he started the scooter, both visitors drew pistols from the folds of their garments and fired at him. He fell onto the scooter. The victim's mother and wife were in the house and witnessed the shooting. The assailants ran away, and the mother heard a vehicle starting on the other side of the road. The mother gave a statement to police, which led to registration of the first information report. The investigating officer called a fingerprint expert to the house. The expert found two glass tumblers on the table, smeared with tea. He lifted fingerprints from them, sealed them in a packet, and sent them to the fingerprint bureau. There, the seal was found intact, and the prints were compared with specimen prints of two suspects taken in the presence of a Judicial Magistrate. The comparison found the questioned prints similar to the specimen prints. The autopsy showed a lacerated wound on the left side of the chest. It had blackening around it and perforated the left lung, the upper part of the heart and the right lung. The doctor opined that death resulted from shock and haemorrhage due to a firearm injury. Police recovered two pistols with live cartridges, two empty twelve-bore cartridges, the scooter and a footwear from the spot.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from a firearm wound to the left chest that perforated the lung and heart
number_of_offences: 3 charged (IPC s.302; IPC s.120-B; Arms Act s.25); 2 finally upheld (IPC s.302 and Arms Act s.25 for the two accused)
premeditation_planning: Not found. The Court found no evidence of conspiracy; the visit was arranged by phone the previous evening.
key_evidence_accepted: Eyewitness testimony of the victim's mother and wife; fingerprint evidence from the tumblers matched to two accused; identification of two accused by the eyewitnesses and by the arrest in their presence; autopsy evidence
witness_credibility: The Court found the mother's and wife's testimonies cogent, natural and trustworthy, with no material discrepancy. The alibi-type contention (absence at a wedding) was rejected because they denied the suggestion and the defence led no evidence. The Court found the eyewitnesses' and fingerprint evidence reliable. It discounted PW9 and doubted PW3's presence.
post_offence_conduct: Not stated (witnesses describe the assailants fleeing immediately; the Court made no finding on post-offence conduct)
bail_history: Bail had been granted to accused Surjit Singh; this Court cancelled it. Other bail history not stated.
trial_duration: offence: 10.11.2002; trial judgment: not given; High Court: 17.09.2007; Supreme Court: 17.12.2014
legal_representation: State of Punjab: V. Madhukar, AAG. Accused: counsel listed for the appearing parties without separating the sides (Anvita Kowshish, Mohit Nain, Dhruv A Mohan, Kuldip Singh and others).
investigation_status: FIR registered; investigation completed; charge sheet filed; 25 prosecution witnesses examined; trial completed
procedural_irregularity: None noted by the Court. The defence alleged no identification parade and non-compliance with s.5 of the Identification of Prisoners Act; the Court rejected the latter as devoid of merit.
appeal_history: Trial court: all seven convicted. High Court: five acquitted; two convictions confirmed. Supreme Court: all appeals dismissed; the two convictions and the five acquittals stand.
prosecution_argument: Not stated in detail. The judgment records only that the State's submissions were heard; the State had challenged the five acquittals.
defence_argument: Complaint did not name the accused; no identification parade; false implication; fingerprints taken after the accused were made to hold tumblers in custody; specimen prints not taken before a Magistrate; presence of the eyewitnesses doubtful because they were at a wedding in another village
legal_principle_applied: Eyewitness testimony assessed for cogency and credibility; omission to name accused in the complaint does not defeat identification by the witnesses; fingerprint evidence corroborates; benefit of doubt for the five acquitted accused
precedent_relied_upon: Mohd. Aman and Anr. vs. State of Rajasthan (1997) 10 SCC 44 (distinguished)
other_sentence_order: Bail of accused Surjit Singh cancelled; he is directed to surrender to serve the remaining sentence
